title: Fix race between approval events and evaluator tick when advancing rollout stages
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: During dogfood/staging we hit a rare but high-impact race where an approval arrives at the same time as the gate evaluator tick. Both paths attempt to advance the rollout stage; depending on ordering, we can (a) advance twice and skip a stage, (b) emit duplicated approval/advance audit events, or (c) wedge the stage state machine with conflicting plan_version expectations. This shows up as rollouts stuck in BETWEEN_STAGES with the console polling forever, or as an unexpected jump from Stage 1 -> Stage 3 when stage weights are non-monotonic. Root cause: stage advancement was effectively "at least once" across two independent workers (approval handler + evaluator), and our optimistic concurrency checks were insufficient because we were checking plan_version but not serializing the "advance" transition itself (approval handler updates approval state, evaluator reads approval state and advances, while approval handler also tries to advance after persisting approval). Changes: (1) Introduce a per-(tenant_id,pool_id,rollout_plan_id) distributed lock around stage advancement. Both evaluator tick and approval handler now call a shared AdvanceStageIfEligible() that acquires the lock (best-effort with bounded wait) before reading latest state and applying a single transition. (2) Add idempotency to advancement by persisting an advance_nonce (uuid) per stage transition and checking for an existing terminal "advanced_to_stage" event for the same from_stage_id + plan_version before writing anything. (3) Tighten write conditions: advancement now requires expected_current_stage_id AND expected_state_version (monotonic counter) in addition to plan_version; if the state version mismatches we re-read under the lock and re-evaluate. (4) Ensure audit/event emission is exactly-once with respect to the persisted transition: audit emission now happens after the state update transaction commits, using the persisted transition_id as the dedupe key in the emitter. Tests: add a deterministic concurrency test that forces approval and evaluator to interleave (barriers) and asserts we advance at most once, do not skip stages, and emit a single stage_advanced audit event; also adds a regression test for repeated approvals (same actor resubmits) to ensure it is a no-op. Notes: This is intentionally conservative (serializes advancement) since Dedicated rollouts have low write QPS but high correctness requirements. Follow-up: once we have more production data, we can consider narrowing lock scope to (plan_id,stage_id) if needed, but current scope matches the routing isolation boundary (pool).
commits: control-plane/rollouts: factor stage advancement into shared helper
control-plane/rollouts: add distributed lock + state_version CAS
audit: emit stage_advanced using transition_id dedupe key
tests: add approval vs evaluator tick race regression
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we avoid locking and rely purely on CAS? Concerned about lock service dependency for advancement path.

Benji Okafor (author): Tried CAS-only; because approval path and evaluator path both need to update different fields and then potentially advance, we still had an interleaving that advanced twice unless we moved to a single transactional update (not feasible with current store). Lock scope is limited to Dedicated pool rollouts and bounded wait; if lock service is degraded we fail safe (no advance).
Jordan Lee (review): Please confirm the routing layer never observes a partially-written state (e.g., stage_id updated but weights not).

Benji Okafor (author): Advancement update is a single store transaction writing current_stage_id + stage_status + transition_id + state_version together. Routing reads from the same snapshot; added a test that polls routing policy evaluation concurrently and ensures it only sees {old_stage} or {new_stage}.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Any RBAC/audit implications? Dedupe key needs to include tenant/pool for exports.

Benji Okafor (author): Yes—transition_id is globally unique, but audit payload includes tenant_id + pool_id + plan_id + from_stage/to_stage + plan_version; emitter dedupes on transition_id only. Export pipeline remains unchanged.
Mina Haddad (review): What happens if we hold the lock, then crash before emitting audit event?
Benji Okafor (author): Audit emission moved post-commit and is retried by the outbox processor keyed by transition_id, so crash after commit is fine (event eventually emitted once).
Ethan Park (review): Requesting change: lock acquisition should be context-bounded and should not block evaluator tick loop forever.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated to 2s max wait and return "not advanced" on timeout. Evaluator will retry next tick; approval handler returns 202 Accepted and console shows "Pending evaluator" if it can’t acquire quickly.
release_notes: Internal: Fixes a race that could cause Dedicated staged rollouts to skip stages or get stuck when approvals arrive concurrently with the gate evaluator tick.
